**Required current destruction-capability signing profile:** `EXT-SECRETS-1` alone custodies the private `DeletionBatchCapabilitySigningKey` family. It signs `DeletionBatchCapabilityV1` as a detached ES256 JWS over RFC 8785 canonical JSON whose closed fields are `Issuer`, committed `EXT-PROTECTION-1` `Audience`, `TenantId`, `DeletionRequestId`, `DestructionSealId`, `BatchKind`, `BatchOrdinal`, `BatchId`, `ManifestDigest`, `GuardStreamId`, `IntendedIssuedGuardRevision`, `AttestationOrdinal`, `SigningAttemptOrdinal`, and `CapabilityKeyVersion`; the actual successful `CommittedIssuedGuardRevision` (`CommittedDestructionSealGuardRevision` for the accepted batch) is recorded separately as result evidence and is excluded from seal id, batch id, signing request id, and signed bytes; the seam publishes the recorded public-anchor id/version and never exposes private material. A target-limited recorded authorization precedes signing, deterministic request lookup resolves loss, and only an exact guard-recorded active attestation is consumable. Routine rotation chooses the current non-revoked version for new issuance and retains every old public verifier through the full referenced batch/outcome lifetime. Emergency compromise publishes an authenticated revocation that immediately blocks unconsumed old-key effects, lets the guard enumerate affected batches, and permits only expected-revision re-attestation of an exactly unconsumed immutable batch under a healthy key: same batch/manifest, next attestation ordinal, old attestation revoked, one active credential. It is not logical capability renewal. Tests cover canonical-byte/header substitution, wrong issuer/audience/tenant, stale/revoked key, lost signing result, routine overlap, compromise before/at/after consume, incomplete enumeration, restore, and no secret leakage.

**Required v23 signing and compromise extension:** The key family is per tenant. Signed bytes contain the once-assigned stable `DestructionSealId`, `IntendedIssuedGuardRevision`, and `SigningAttemptOrdinal`; `DeletionBatchCapabilitySigningRequestId` binds all three with batch, manifest, attestation, key version, and audience. If conditional issue loses, only exact guard no-issue proof permits terminal `SignedAttestationObsoleteUnissued`; a successor pre-issue attempt retains stable seal id/batch/manifest/attestation ordinal, increments signing attempt, and binds the returned current guard revision/current healthy key. Two or more consecutive stale attempts change only signing-attempt ordinal, intended revision, and—if rotation requires—the current healthy key; the actual successful issue revision remains separate. Unknown signer/issue outcome cannot retry. Emergency re-attestation remains post-issue only and requires an authenticated protection-owner `ConsumptionBlocked(CapabilityKeyCompromise)` receipt. The authenticated emergency-revocation envelope binds issuer, audience, tenant, key family/version, revocation revision, trust-profile revision, event identity, and signature digest for the non-public registrar; duplicates/lost acknowledgement use exact lookup and cross-tenant or changed evidence rejects. The registrar cannot request a signature, mint an attestation, or act as a human Platform/Workflow principal.

acceptedFields.RequiredArtifact: Platform-owned host composition for the Agents DomainService and UI with EventStore, Conversations, Parties, Tenants, Provider and safety adapters, Dapr Workflow, secrets, health, identity, telemetry, and a replicated durable content-free `security-audit-spool`. The spool accepts a deterministic `SecurityObservationId` before a classified Agents denial returns, retains pending records across EventStore/replay outages, exposes exact-id outcome lookup/acknowledgement, and grants its drain worker an ACL restricted to the computed `SecurityEventLog(RoutingTenantId, UtcDay)` stream and event; if the spool itself is unavailable, ingress constructs no Agents command and platform health blocks tenant-access/audit readiness. The host additionally binds the production `EXT-PROTECTION-1` engine and exposes the FR-34 attestation port used at startup and every readiness evaluation. The port lets Agents seal a canary, prove persisted bytes contain no plaintext, unseal it, destroy its DEK, replay `Erased`, and obtain engine identity/version for comparison with the committed protection target; the host fails closed against both the no-op default and a self-reporting wrapper around it. For Story 6.1 it also composes the target-limited directory-migration Workflow and EventStore namespace ports. Installing a tenant migration epoch revokes the legacy direct-write credential/epoch, and every later interaction/failure create or content append requires the current epoch plus an exact directory permit or committed-effect capability. Every `ConversationAgentState` permit, creation/workflow-start/User-action-intent outbox, lease acquire/commit, and interaction-owned rate/open/Budget/capacity phase-authorization append is likewise conditional on the current directory capability at EventStore. Repair first atomically installs a directory-repair fence that revokes all those new-directory/effect-authorization operations and returns an authenticated checkpoint; only the post-fence finite permit/outbox/lease/phase-authorization cohort may enter the old-epoch bridge, whose exact pending/committed/authorized work drains before successor activation revokes the old epoch, repair fence, and bridge. For Story 8.3 the same port evaluates canonical `GovernanceScopeV1` and its predicate digest from authoritative tenant stream identity, immutable first-event/directory-permit `SourceConversationId`, and permit/action/lease/phase-authorization owner facts—never caller classification. Before either deletion origin builds a candidate, it conditionally installs a persistent ordinal scope admission fence that rejects later matching permit, User-action-intent, lease-acquire/commit, and rate/open/Budget/capacity phase-authorization appends; after the finite same-ordinal owner cycles become Effective it conditionally installs and verifies the separate content write fence that rejects later matching interaction/failure creates or content appends. The admission violation ledger is one append-only request ledger partitioned by fence ordinal: prior violations remain visible, while only the current installed ordinal can attest `ZeroAcceptedViolationsSinceInstall`. A pre-cut violation uses an explicit no-global-cut/candidate/token receipt; a later violation invalidates only exact present artifacts. Both assign one successor ordinal and require separately keyed owner cycles carrying all prior obligations. The content guard is stable by request/predicate and continuously installed: after one or more recuts, a successor-binding authorize/effect/result operation starts from the latest installed binding and appends the new ordinal/global-cut/token only after proving a complete gap-free ordered chain of intervening invalidated/tokenless ordinal receipts and the current zero proof; an overtaken authorization returns terminal obsolete without a guard append. The port also owns the tenant `GovernanceScopeGuard`: every authorized legal-hold request conditionally registers its canonical scope there before fence preparation and remains until an exact fully acknowledged release removes it. Hold registration and `CommitDeletionDestructionStartBarrierEffect` serialize on that owner. The `ProtectionFence` barrier authorization persists the exact observed `GovernanceScopeGuard` revision/compare token. Conditional append at that revision makes the seal operation serialize with admission writes and hold registration/release; an intervening mutation returns authenticated stale and must be mirrored before revision-bound reauthorization. The seal operation verifies both ledgers/current content binding/migration receipts, rejects any overlapping contender that won after authorization unless it consumes the exact effective deletion-allowed hold disposition, commits immutable `DestructionSealed`, and returns one deterministic non-expiring, revocable, single-use `DestroyDekManifest` capability bound to the sorted accepted key-target manifest; it has no `ExpiresAt` or renewal branch, and its capability-key version remains verifiable through outage, migration, restore, and the full retention of the batch identity and terminal outcome, including exact retry/lookup after consumption or revocation. No direct clean read, stale no-hold authorization, or unrelated append is authority. Each fence/guard/barrier exposes authenticated installation, exact-outcome lookup, verification/high-water, and complete append-only evidence; every admission ordinal/violation gap chain, owner cycle, content binding, hold contender/release, barrier/containment compare authorization and stale result, destruction seal, and batch identity/capability-key/guard-issued state plus referenced protection-owner blocked, reserved, re-attested, consumed, or revoked outcome survives migration successors. The protection engine consumes each manifest batch atomically as all targets or none, returns an ordered per-target irreversible receipt vector, and exposes exact batch lookup; each first previously uncovered complete protection target from an authoritative post-seal content violation is ProtectionFence-serialized into one monotonic ordinal and immutable singleton target manifest, while later same-target resources receive coverage links only, then follows `AuthorizeDeletionContainmentBatch`, guard-revision-conditional `CommitDeletionContainmentBatchEffect`, exact lookup, and `RecordDeletionContainmentBatchIssued` or `RecordDeletionContainmentBatchIssuanceStale` before its distinct batch may be consumed; exact duplicates reuse the ordinal/result and concurrent distinct targets receive distinct ordinals. An accepted admission after sealing invokes `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption` to race `ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch` at the protection owner, records `DeletionIntegrityCompromised`, blocks new batches, and can never be treated as resource-only content containment or successful completion. Missing, malformed, unknown-version, cross-tenant, or unverifiable scope membership rejects a write and prevents a clean verification result. The artifact replaces module-owned AppHost, Aspire, and ServiceDefaults ownership.
acceptedFields.CompatibilityContractAndVerificationComm: Contract: clean-checkout composition through the platform host without module-owned hosting infrastructure, including the durable security-audit spool, production protection-engine binding, and complete FR-34 attestation. The target-limited migration contract enforces the current epoch on interaction, directory, and effect-authorization writes; provides atomic directory-repair-fence install/checkpoint/lookup; freezes only the post-boundary cohort including protected User-action intents and rate/open/Budget/capacity authorizations; restricts the bridge to manifest-listed pending, committed, or already-authorized work; preserves every deletion fence ordinal/violation gap chain, owner-cycle receipt, continuous content binding, guard compare authorization/stale result, destruction seal, and batch capability/state; and atomically revokes old epoch/repair fence/bridge at successor activation. The deletion contract implements canonical exact-interaction and source-deletion exact-Conversation predicates; ordinal admission-fence authorize/effect/result; explicit pre-cut and post-cut violation containment with one successor ordinal; immutable separately keyed owner cycles and current zero proof; one continuously installed predicate content guard whose successor binding uses the latest installed binding plus a gap-free invalidation chain and returns terminal obsolete when overtaken; tenant-scope-guard revision/compare-token hold registration/release serialized with the destruction seal and authenticated stale reauthorization; an exact effective armed-contention disposition only when required; guard-owned atomic start-barrier authorize/effect/result; deterministic non-expiring, revocable, all-or-none manifest-batch destruction with per-target vectors, exact lookup and revocation race; guard-owned singleton containment-batch authorize/effect/result with ordinal allocation and lost-issuance lookup; migration preservation; post-start integrity blocking; and content containment with distinct batches. Tests race every directory/phase-authorization append and target write around migration-repair, admission-fence, and destruction-barrier boundaries; cover violations before the first cut and after content-fence installation; prove one successor ordinal, carried obligations, immutable Effective, repeated recut gap chains/obsolete binding outcomes, continuous content binding, and current zero; race hold registration/release before/at/after guard-revision-bound barrier authorization/seal while Open precedence stalls both and stale compare results require reauthorization; prove the guard commit—not a prior read—is first irreversible authority; and prove an exact multi-key manifest batch is consumed once, all targets or none, with non-expiring restore, lost-result lookup, revocation, explicit singleton containment issuance/lookup, and prior violations preserved. Human-origin exact-Conversation tests remain blocked pending `OD-HUMAN-EXACT-CONVERSATION-SCOPE-1`; `ClassUtcRange` tests remain blocked pending `OD-GOVERNANCE-CLASS-RANGE-SCOPE-1`.
